factorial_interaction.definition: (corrected DIN - ordinary DIN) - (corrected pool - ordinary pool)
factorial_interaction.interpretation: Attention attenuates the observed AUC penalty of full count correction. A positive AUC interaction does not mean corrected DIN beats ordinary DIN. The Logloss interaction is much smaller. This descriptive interaction has no estimated uncertainty.

observations.statement: History pooling improves AUC over static features by 0.0052224992242449, and target-aware attention improves over pooling by 0.0031358724110028. Both changes also lower overall Logloss. History and target conditioning therefore have local predictive value under this recipe.

Both ordinary arms reproduce their corresponding ancestors exactly in aggregate AUC, Logloss, and every reported slice metric, at identical parameter counts. This supports use of the ordinary arms as bridges for intervention attribution.

Full count correction lowers AUC and raises Logloss in both branches. The pooled penalty is -0.0017334134126946 AUC / +0.0000367396712915 Logloss; the DIN penalty is -0.0001905059724607 AUC / +0.0000314515662284 Logloss.
observations.outcome: negative for the proposed full-correction performance benefit

observations.statement: The AUC difference-in-differences is +0.0015429074402339. Target-aware scoring substantially attenuates the correction penalty in this seed; it does not reverse the overall ranking.

The diagnostic intervention is active: at the ordinary DIN checkpoint, mean pv attention mass conditional on pv presence changes from 0.829869 under ordinary weights to 0.323921 under corrected weights. The corrected-trained checkpoint has 0.965264 under ordinary counterfactual weights and 0.673296 under its active corrected weights. These are two normalizations per checkpoint; cross-checkpoint differences also include learned representation changes. Per-type reported means use different presence-conditioned denominators and must not be summed as a probability partition.
observations.scope: Candidate-supplied, first 512 validation impressions, not independently verified

observations.statement: Diagnostics cover 4 empty, 40 single-type and 468 mixed-type histories; 395/468 mixed histories have at least 90% pv events. Padding mass is zero and maximum normalization error is at most 2.3842e-7. Single-type summary perturbation is about 3e-7 to 4e-7 for DIN, consistent with subtracting a common log-count leaving softmax weights invariant. This is a narrow implementation sanity check, not population evidence or a relevance assessment.

Corrected DIN gains +0.0003955323 AUC on category_match_absent (717,129 samples / 29,616 positives / 687,513 negatives), while Logloss worsens by +0.0000537532; category_match_present loses -0.0003253239 AUC. The diagnostic category-absent subset also includes 16 brand-present histories among 134 nonempty category-absent histories. Category absence cannot be interpreted as absence of all useful evidence.

Corrected DIN loses -0.0015670382 AUC for history_1_16 and -0.0009893867 for history_17_64, but only -0.0000234989 for history_gt64. The longest slice contains 93.5849% of validation impressions. Global AUC includes cross-slice positive-negative pairs, so it cannot be decomposed as a sample-weighted sum of slice AUCs.

On empty histories corrected DIN improves +0.0019564707 AUC and -0.0017289143 Logloss, although the normalization has no direct event-weight intervention there. The 8,272 impressions contain only 310 positives. End-to-end retraining changes shared parameters, so empty/single-type cross-model changes do not establish a direct normalization effect.

Corrected DIN worsens AUC in the four supplied frequency groups below 100 and improves it by +0.0006541180 in the highest-frequency group, where Logloss worsens +0.0000913672. No calibration or frequency-specific mechanism is established by these aggregate divergences.

All seven supplied trials have success status and null errors. There is no supplied execution-failure or abandoned-implementation receipt. The unsuccessful scientific branches are full correction in pooling and full correction in DIN; they remain in the analysis. Baseline and bridge reruns use the same seed and do not constitute independent support.

interpretations.claim: Behavior multiplicity can dominate the normalization without being a harmful bias. Removing multiplicity changed summaries and hurt overall prediction in this setting.
interpretations.status: provisional explanation; full-correction benefit unsupported

interpretations.claim: Learned target-aware scores may compensate for, or be less sensitive to, the imposed count correction. The smaller DIN penalty and higher uncorrected pv mass in the corrected-trained model are consistent with adaptation.
interpretations.status: provisional; descriptive attention weights are not proof of causal relevance
alternatives: The correction acts as an optimization perturbation.
Different embedding geometry changes both scores and summary scale.
Seed-specific variation explains some or all of the small DIN gap.

interpretations.claim: The count-normalization mechanism was implemented sufficiently to perturb attention, but the causal claim that reducing frequent-action dominance improves full-population prediction lacks support. This does not refute all behavior-aware aggregation or a weaker correction.
interpretations.status: single-seed controlled negative result with limited diagnostics

interpretations.claim: Category-absent AUC gains and improved rare-action-absent slices motivate questions rather than subgroup deployment or a new architecture. AUC/Logloss disagreement, overlapping groups and small diagnostic subsets leave the relevance mechanism unresolved.

prior_work_and_difference.inherited_components: Per receipt notes: existing static and history representations, target-aware scorer for DIN, softmax normalization, classifier, initialization/module construction, optimizer/loss, fields and causal history interface. prior_work_and_difference.proposed_and_tested_difference: For each valid visible event i of type b, replace its attention logit s_i by s_i - log(n_b), where n_b is the visible masked within-type count. With pooled scores this becomes equal mass per present type and uniform mass within type. With target-aware scores it normalizes each type total by its count; it does not force equal type masses.

next_action.action: Retain baseline-din; prepare a bounded partial-correction study for a later authorized experiment phase. Do not train or modify models during this analyze phase.
next_action.observation: Full correction substantially hurts pooling and slightly hurts DIN, despite active diagnostic changes; the smaller DIN penalty may indicate compensation or overcorrection.
next_action.mechanism_hypothesis: A fixed half-strength count correction preserves useful intensity while attenuating type multiplicity, avoiding some of the penalty of full correction. Target-aware scoring may account for the attenuation of the penalty.
next_action.nearest_existing_work: Use the ordinary and full-corrected local factorial as the immediate controls. Search and inspect primary work on behavior-wise normalization before asserting a literature difference; no priority claim is needed for this follow-up.
next_action.inherited_components: Keep existing embeddings, fields, history masks/limit, scorer, classifier, parameter construction/order, training recipe, initialization policy and causal boundaries.
next_action.proposed_difference: Use s_i - alpha*log(n_b), with one predeclared interior alpha=0.5 and existing endpoints alpha=0 and alpha=1. No learned gate, new count feature, history expansion or optimizer change.
controls_and_order: At seed 42, add only half-corrected pooling and half-corrected DIN. Reuse the four completed endpoint arms only after matching source/config/protocol/data identity and preserving parameter initialization order. This completes a descriptive attention-by-strength 2x3 comparison.

Run ordinary, half-corrected and full-corrected DIN at paired seeds 43 and 44 (six jobs). Together with seed 42 this estimates seed variation for the consequential DIN comparison. Pooling interaction remains single-seed unless a later predeclared repetition is justified.

For each checkpoint, retain the existing label-free normalization diagnostics and, if supported by the authorized interface, report ordinary/half/full weights at the same checkpoint to separate algebraic intervention from retraining. Preserve the first-512 caveat; do not assume a new sampling interface exists.
Do not introduce adaptive coefficients, additional variants or subgroup selection based on these results without a new prospective record. Never use withheld outcomes for continuation.
predicted_observations: Under a strength-related overcorrection explanation, alpha=0.5 should recover some of the alpha=1 AUC penalty while giving intermediate frequent-type mass at a fixed checkpoint.

A useful partial correction would beat alpha=0 on the primary validation objective with consistent paired-seed direction; a ranking-only gain with worse Logloss remains a tradeoff, not an unqualified benefit.
If target-aware scores compensate, DIN may show a flatter strength-response than pooling. This is a provisional interaction prediction, and it could also arise from optimization differences.
next_action.falsifying_evidence: Half correction does not recover the full-correction penalty, or ordinary DIN remains superior across paired seeds. A non-repeating interaction undermines the compensation explanation. Close the full-count-correction branch after this bounded study if neither mechanism nor performance is supported; retain all negative results.

observations.statement: The static, pooled and target-aware references have AUC 0.6050036145, 0.6102261137 and 0.6133619861. Pooling and target conditioning each improve both overall metrics at seed 42. Ordinary round-one controls exactly reproduce the corresponding reported reference metrics and slices.

All nine supplied trials succeeded operationally, including both latest arms. Full correction is a negative performance trajectory, not a failed execution: AUC falls by 0.0017334134 for pooling and 0.0001905060 for DIN, with worse Logloss in both. No failed execution receipt or additional abandoned branch is supplied.

Latest half-corrected pooling reaches AUC 0.6108065192 and Logloss 0.1969882654: changes of +0.0005804055 and -0.0000981980 against ordinary pooling. It recovers and exceeds the full-correction pooling penalty, but remains below ordinary DIN by 0.0025554669 AUC and has higher Logloss.

Latest half-corrected DIN reaches AUC 0.6131537618 and Logloss 0.1968125047: changes of -0.0002082243 and +0.0000178582 against ordinary DIN. Against full correction, AUC is lower by 0.0000177184 while Logloss improves by 0.0000135933. Thus half strength does not rescue the primary DIN objective in this seed.

The attention-by-correction AUC interaction is +0.0015429074 at full strength but -0.0007886299 at half strength. The original positive interaction does not extend uniformly over strength. DIN has a relatively flat three-point response while pooling is nonmonotonic; three points do not identify an optimum or response curve.

Latest candidate-supplied first-512 diagnostics show active alpha=0.5, zero padding mass, weight-sum error at most 2.3842e-7, zero empty summary, and near-invariant conditional within-type weights and single-type weights. Mixed-history mean half-versus-ordinary summary L2 changes are 1.0636960 for pooling and 1.1264205 for DIN. These support an active between-type redistribution in this limited sample, not a causal performance explanation.

At the half-DIN checkpoint, mean pv mass conditional on pv presence is 0.9295267 under ordinary normalization, 0.7707562 under half, and 0.4762428 under full correction. The corresponding half-pooling values are 0.9447256, 0.7888888 and 0.4281723. These are same-checkpoint counterfactual normalizations, not three retrained model performance measurements. Type-specific means use different presence denominators and must not be summed.

The diagnostic sample contains 4 empty, 40 single-type and 468 mixed-type histories; 395 mixed histories have at least 90% pv share. It is the first 512 ordered impressions, not a random population sample. Raw DIN score means differ across trained checkpoints and are not comparable evidence of compensation without centered, matched-input analysis.

Half pooling improves AUC and Logloss in each of four hour bins, but not every slice: past-buy-present AUC and the lowest user-frequency AUC decline. In category-match-absent impressions its AUC increases by 0.0009956346 while Logloss worsens by 0.0000363654. Half DIN instead loses category-absent AUC by 0.0004225199, reversing the full-DIN exploratory gain of 0.0003955323; Logloss worsens for both corrected DIN strengths in that slice.

Half DIN improves empty-history AUC by 0.0048421535 and Logloss by 0.0009431824 despite zero empty summaries in diagnostics. Such changes can arise through shared parameter training; they cannot be attributed to direct reweighting of empty histories. The slice has only 310 positive exposures. All three nonempty length bins have lower half-DIN AUC than ordinary DIN.

All six normalization arms report 17,130,275 parameters, including the unused attention module in pooling controls. Half pooling uses 455.44 training seconds and 430,361,088 peak GPU bytes; half DIN uses 491.36 seconds and 654,937,600 bytes. This is a matched-recipe/capacity comparison, not measured equal compute. Shorter round-two times occur in both branches and do not establish a correction-specific speedup.

limitations: Only seed 42 is measured. Aggregate summaries cannot yield paired user-cluster confidence intervals; identical bridge metrics do not supply independent repetitions.

All slice analysis is exploratory. Counts are supplied in the complete slice table. No invented sufficiency threshold is imposed; empty-history (310 positives), pv-absent (397) and frequency-1_2 (1045) slices need particular caution. Positive exposure counts are not independent user counts.

The model window is capped at 128 visible events. No claim is made about complete lifetime behavior, omitted events, or unavailable item identities.
AUC is not additive over slices. Improved slice AUC with worse Logloss alone does not diagnose probability calibration.

observations.statement: Pooling improves AUC over static by 0.0052224992, and target-aware attention adds 0.0031358724 over pooling. Both also lower Logloss. This establishes useful histories and target conditioning for the local references; it does not identify a query or field bottleneck.

Full count correction loses AUC in pooling (-0.0017334134) and DIN (-0.0001905060), and worsens Logloss in both. Half correction improves pooling (+0.0005804055 AUC, -0.0000981980 Logloss) but loses DIN AUC (-0.0002082243). Half DIN is also below full DIN AUC. These operationally successful negative interventions must be retained.

The attention-by-count-correction AUC interaction changes from +0.0015429074 at full strength to -0.0007886299 at half strength. Frequent-type mass and summaries change in diagnostics, yet usefulness is branch dependent. This qualifies the older attention-compensation explanation.

All 13 supplied model trials report success and null errors. No failed model execution is exposed. Scientific negatives, missing inputs, preparation/source-access failures and successful host training are different statuses.

The latest joint restriction has AUC 0.6144940344 and Logloss 0.1966904258. Relative to the latest ordinary product, changes are +0.0011629547 AUC and -0.0001788009 Logloss; relative to historical DIN, +0.0011320483 and -0.0001042207. These are single-seed validation results.

Removing cross products alone improves both metrics at either context setting: AUC +0.0009657589 with context retained and +0.0006829896 with context removed; Logloss -0.0001967024 and -0.0003059556. Context removal improves AUC at either cross setting (+0.0004799650 and +0.0001971958), but worsens Logloss (+0.0001271547 and +0.0000179014). The cross-removal arm has the best Logloss among the four latest arms.

The cross-by-context AUC interaction is -0.0002827692: the joint AUC gain is subadditive, not positive synergy. The Logloss interaction is -0.0001092532, favorable on the lower-is-better scale, but context removal still increases Logloss at both settings. The interaction does not eliminate the joint-versus-cross Logloss tradeoff.

The ordinary-product bridge differs from historical DIN by -0.0000309064 AUC and +0.0000745803 Logloss. Slice differences are larger in some small groups; empty-history AUC differs by +0.0028066785. Exact source/operation-equivalence assertions in submission notes are not established by the supplied host outcomes.

Latest diagnostics show declared factor flags, zero padding mass and zero empty summaries, weight normalization error at most 1.78814e-7, and product decomposition relative error at most 3.93581e-7. These are candidate-authored checks on the first 512 ordered validation impressions, not independent full-population certification.

At the ordinary-product checkpoint, removing cross products changes mean attention L1 by 0.4398596, history-summary L2 by 1.1341075 and absolute logit by 0.0782455 over nonempty diagnostic examples. The joint change gives 0.5811910, 1.5538177 and 0.1084849. Both category-match and brand-match mass rise under that joint counterfactual. This shows numerical activity at a fixed checkpoint; no counterfactual full-validation predictive score is supplied.

The diagnostic subset has 508 nonempty and 4 empty impressions, 374 category matches, 145 brand matches, 129 both, 245 category-only, 16 brand-only and 118 neither. There are 51 target-brand-zero impressions and no zero target categories. Match-mass means condition on different sets and cannot be summed or interpreted as relevance labels.

The joint arm improves AUC and Logloss in all four reported hour bins and both category-match slices relative to the latest ordinary arm, but loses both metrics in empty-history and pv-absent slices. Empty: 8272 exposures/310 positives, delta AUC -0.0021201514, delta Logloss +0.0004096582; pv-absent: 10998/397, delta AUC -0.0022802136, delta Logloss +0.0008753525. These overlapping exploratory groups do not justify a gate.

The joint arm gains AUC and lowers Logloss in all three nonempty length bins; history_gt64 contains 3026583 of 3234051 impressions. It is not universally strongest within slices: cross removal has better Logloss in several groups and better AUC in the two lowest reported user-frequency bins. Overall AUC cannot be reconstructed by averaging slice AUC.

All latest arms have 17130275 parameters (17078688 embedding; 51587 dense). Their training times span 505.87 to 526.05 seconds, wall times 593.72 to 614.37, and peak GPU bytes 801711616 to 828414464. Joint versus ordinary uses slightly more wall/train time and nearly equal peak memory. Relative to historical DIN, memory rises from 654936064 to 802390016 bytes. Timing/memory include differing code or diagnostic execution conditions; no equal-compute or speedup claim follows.

prior_work_and_difference.reported_local_mechanism: Let q=target-category + target-brand and h_i=history-category + history-brand + action/recency context. observations.statement: Baseline histories are useful: pooled minus static AUC is +0.0052224992; DIN minus pooled is +0.0031358724, with lower Logloss in both. This does not isolate a field/query bottleneck.

Full count correction loses AUC and Logloss in both pooling and DIN. Half correction improves pooling (+0.0005804055 AUC) but reduces DIN AUC (-0.0002082243), slightly below full-corrected DIN. The bounded partial-correction follow-up did not rescue the target-aware branch.

Round-3 joint restriction leads primary validation AUC at 0.6144940344272417, Logloss 0.19669042580912716. It improves AUC by 0.0011629546942916394 over its ordinary adapter and 0.0011320483081733723 over historical DIN. Relative to historical DIN Logloss falls by 0.00010422066570520139.

Cross-field removal improves both metrics at either context setting. Context-product removal increases AUC but worsens Logloss at either cross setting. Joint minus cross-only AUC is +0.00019719580032073747 and Logloss is +0.000017901439788470253. Thus cross-only is a consequential comparator and both restrictions are not required for an improvement.
The 2x2 AUC interaction is -0.00028276924606862597: joint gains are subadditive. The Logloss interaction is -0.00010925323629681905 on a lower-is-better scale. No positive AUC synergy is supported.

Round 4 exactly reproduces each historical path's reported AUC, Logloss and all slice counts/metrics: historical baseline, ordinary adapter and joint adapter. The baseline-adapter offset persists at -0.00003090638611826746 AUC and +0.00007458025739059175 Logloss. Replays narrow the explanation toward a stable implementation/training-path difference; they do not identify its cause or certify source equivalence.

The new inline joint realization exactly matches the adapter joint's reported AUC, Logloss, every reported slice, and all 57 common diagnostic keys. Its extra inline_helper_logit_abs_max is 0 on the first 512 validation impressions. This supports limited implementation consistency. It is neither a new mechanism nor an independent seed.

The inline joint versus original inline baseline therefore retains the +0.0011320483 AUC gain in an alternative implementation path reported to follow the baseline forward structure. This weakens an explanation attributing the entire gain solely to the ordinary adapter's mismatch, conditional on receipt-described isolation. Unexposed source and training traces prevent a full audit.

Candidate-authored diagnostics show active attention/summary/logit changes under same-checkpoint product interventions, with zero padding mass/empty summary, normalization errors <=1.78814e-7 and product-decomposition errors <=3.93581e-7 in the product quartet. These measure numerical activity on 512 ordered impressions, not semantic relevance or causal mediation of the score gain.

Joint improves both metrics against the ordinary adapter in all nonempty length bins, four hour bins, category-match bins, and reported frequency bins. It loses both metrics in empty_history (8272/310 positives) and past_pv_absent (10998/397 positives). Those losses recur exactly in round-4 replays, which add no independent subgroup support. Against historical baseline the empty-history AUC direction differs (+0.0006865271), while Logloss still worsens; subgroup claims depend on the comparator.

All compared history models have 17130275 parameters: 17078688 embedding and 51587 dense. Inline joint peak allocation is 738064384 bytes versus adapter joint 802390016 (-64325632, approximately 8.0%), but exceeds inline baseline's 654936064. Inline joint training/wall time is 519.64/611.16 seconds versus adapter replay 527.97/620.68; this is one timing comparison with different diagnostic paths, not an equal-compute efficiency result.

All 17 exposed trajectory entries report execution success; the 15 direct detailed receipts have null errors. The two missing detailed pooling receipts are supplemented from scoped prior memory, with current index confirmation of status/AUC/wall time. No failed host model execution is exposed. Negative count-correction results are scientific negatives, not missing data or execution failures.

candidate_diagnostics.interpretation_boundary: Unit norm checks cover the explicit fourth scorer block and sampled nonfloored events, not all inputs or training. Diagnostics compare each operation to aligned raw within a checkpoint. Cross-checkpoint match mass and norm differences confound adaptation. observations.statement: Pooled history improves AUC over static features by 0.0052224992; target-aware history adds 0.0031358724 over pooling. Both reduce Logloss. This establishes useful baseline history signal, not a specific semantic matching mechanism.

Full count correction hurts both pooling and DIN. Half correction helps pooling (+0.0005804055 AUC) but not DIN (-0.0002082243); full-corrected DIN is also below ordinary (-0.0001905060). The bounded partial-correction follow-up did not rescue the target-aware branch. All are successful executions with scientific negative outcomes, not failed jobs.

In round 3, removing explicit cross-field products improves both metrics at either context setting. Context-product removal raises AUC but worsens Logloss at either cross setting. The AUC interaction is negative (-0.0002827692), so the joint gain is subadditive. Both restrictions are not necessary for an improvement.

Round-4 replays exactly match their source paths on all reported aggregate and slice metrics. Inline joint matches adapter joint, with zero helper logit discrepancy on the first 512 impressions. Original baseline and ordinary adapter remain different (-0.0000309064 adapter AUC, +0.0000745803 Logloss). This is stable seed-42 path dependence without identified root cause.

Latest normalized aligned candidate has AUC 0.6149816911798147 and Logloss 0.19656340759133067 on 3,234,051 validation exposures (159,437 positives). It leads all 20 supplied trial entries in AUC and all 20 recovered detailed rows in Logloss; repeated rows do not supply independent support.

Aligned normalization improves AUC by 0.0004876568 and reduces Logloss by 0.0001270182 versus raw aligned. Crossed normalization changes AUC by only +0.0000139449 and worsens Logloss by +0.0002459431. A universal benefit from product normalization is not observed.

Aligned beats crossed by +0.0011162489 AUC with raw products and +0.0015899607 with unit products; Logloss also favors aligned in both. Alignment-by-normalization AUC interaction is +0.0004737118 and Logloss interaction -0.0003729613. This differs from round-3 subadditivity because the factors are different.

Latest-minus-original-DIN AUC is +0.0016197051 and Logloss -0.0002312389; latest also improves both metrics versus the earlier context-retaining cross-removal arm. The aggregate AUC/Logloss tradeoff between the earlier joint and context-retaining restriction is no longer a reason to prefer either over the latest candidate at seed 42.

Latest supplied diagnostics report unit product norm 1.0, maximum unit norm error 1.78814e-7, aligned/crossed unit norm difference <=2.38419e-7, zero padding mass, zero empty summary and zero forward/helper logit error on the first 512 impressions. All 60,475 visible valid events are nonfloored in both products. Unit aligned/crossed directions differ (mean cosines -0.02531, +0.00495, -0.00628 in the three trained checkpoints).

Normalization at the aligned-unit checkpoint changes weights, summaries and logits relative to aligned-raw counterfactuals (mean nonempty weight L1 1.59829, summary L2 5.57161, absolute logit change 0.45850). These are diagnostic activity measurements, not counterfactual validation scores or causal mediation. All diagnostic variants are referenced to aligned raw, not each checkpoint active model.

Latest improves both metrics over raw aligned in 21 of 23 supplied slices, but loses both in history_17_64 (157391 samples/6311 positives) and user_train_frequency_100_4294967296 (1004912/33140). It improves AUC and Logloss over original DIN in all 23 slices. It beats crossed-unit AUC in all 23, but has worse Logloss in empty_history, past_pv_absent and the highest frequency bin. These are exploratory overlapping summaries.

Latest recovers the raw-aligned empty-history and pv-absent losses, but zero history summaries mean empty-history changes cannot directly demonstrate better history-event matching; training of shared representations/classifier can change these scores.

All history arms report 17,130,275 parameters (17,078,688 embedding; 51,587 dense). Latest wall/train times are 614.783/524.601 seconds, peak GPU allocation 832,739,328 bytes, throughput 179,887.75 examples/s and whole-batch p95 22.135 ms at batch size 4096 including feature gathering. Latest versus raw aligned increases peak allocation 3.78% and train time 1.94%; versus original DIN increases peak allocation 27.15% with similar train time. Single-run timing does not establish an efficiency frontier.

All 20 trajectory entries report operational success; all 15 directly supplied detailed receipts have null errors. Five older detailed receipts are available only in scoped agent-r0004 memory and are marked as such. No failed host model run is exposed, and no unseen failure is invented.

prior_work_and_difference.local_algebra: Let q_c,q_b be target category/brand vectors; h_c,h_b history category/brand vectors; u action/recency context. D=q_c*h_c+q_b*h_b (aligned), X=q_c*h_b+q_b*h_c (crossed), C=(q_c+q_b)*u, with * elementwise. Ordinary product block is D+X+C. Round-3 flags form D+(1-A)X+(1-B)C. r0003-cross_only REMOVES X and retains D+C; it is NOT the r0005 crossed replacement, which uses X alone. r0003-context_only removes C and retains D+X. Raw aligned is D; latest unit aligned normalizes D by its per-event L2 norm with an implementation floor; crossed arms replace D by X with raw or unit normalization. Exact floor constant/source is not exposed. Other scorer blocks and history values retain context and learned mixed-field interactions.
prior_work_and_difference.mechanism_difference: Count correction changes s_i to s_i-alpha*log(n_type), affecting between-type attention mass. Product restriction/replacement instead changes one explicit target-history interaction block. Unit normalization changes that block magnitude and gradients; it is neither count balancing nor softmax removal. No supplied trial combines these mechanisms.

observations.observation: All 23 supplied model trajectories succeeded operationally. Full count correction loses AUC for pooling (-0.0017334134) and DIN (-0.0001905060). Half correction improves pooling (+0.0005804055) but loses DIN AUC (-0.0002082243). Half pooling remains below DIN. These are negative or limited scientific outcomes, not failed execution.

Round-3 joint product restriction improved AUC over its ordinary adapter by 0.0011629547; removing cross-field products alone nearly matched it. The joint version had slightly worse Logloss than the cross-field-removal-only arm. Round-4 replays preserved the reported outcomes, while baseline versus ordinary adapter retained a small numerical-path discrepancy. This supports local behavior, not universal benefit from both removals.

The round-6 same-body aligned/raw bridge exactly reproduces historical raw aligned AUC, Logloss and every supplied slice metric/count at seed 42. Its source hash differs. This narrows the earlier mixed-round raw-corner uncertainty at the outcome level; source and backward identity remain unverified.

Full-gradient normalized aligned remains the validation incumbent: AUC 0.6149816911798147, Logloss 0.19656340759133067. Detached aligned reaches AUC 0.6145833321081287, Logloss 0.19663658831646288. Full-minus-detached is +0.00039835907168606077 AUC and -0.0000731807251322103 Logloss. Detached aligned still beats aligned raw by +0.00008929768088694612 AUC and -0.00005383749266427151 Logloss.

Crossed full-minus-detached AUC is +0.00004607634386211146 but Logloss is worse by 0.00012588645933467313. The pairing-by-gradient interaction is +0.0003522827278239493 AUC and -0.00019906718446688343 Logloss. Alignment still wins under either gradient rule and under raw products.

Both detached checkpoints report identical same-state full/detached products and logits (max absolute differences zero). Candidate diagnostics show zero padding mass, zero empty summary, weight-sum errors <=1.1920928955078125e-7 and unit-product norm errors <=1.7881393432617188e-7. No floor cases occur in 60,475 visible events among the first 512 impressions. Backward correctness and population absence of floor cases are not measured.

Full aligned is not uniformly best. In the highest training-frequency slice (1,004,912 impressions, 33,140 positives), its AUC 0.6365456862 is below detached 0.6365801374 and raw 0.6367937224. In history_17_64 (157,391 impressions, 6,311 positives), full aligned loses both metrics to raw. Empty-history changes have only 310 positives and zero direct history summaries; shared training effects are plausible.

All detailed interaction models have 17,130,275 parameters (17,078,688 embedding; 51,587 dense). Full-unit peak GPU bytes are 832,739,328 versus 800,846,848 detached. Their training times span about 521-529 seconds. Single-run timing and memory are observations; no equal-compute frontier or production throughput gain is established.

prior_work_and_difference.inherited_components: Per receipts: static/history embeddings; category/brand/action/recency features; target-aware scorer, masked softmax aggregation, history values and classifier; optimizer/loss, initialization policy and training/data recipe. prior_work_and_difference.local_algebra: Let D=q_c*h_c+q_b*h_b, X=q_c*h_b+q_b*h_c, C=(q_c+q_b)*u, with * elementwise and u action/recency context. Ordinary product block is D+X+C. Round-3 cross_only REMOVES X and retains D+C; it is not the round-5/6 crossed replacement X alone. Unit normalization is z=p/max(||p||_2,epsilon), with p=D or X; exact floor constant is unexposed. Latest detached intervention stops only the denominator derivative. Other blocks/history values retain context and mixed-field information. No new parameters are added.
prior_work_and_difference.gradient_hypothesis: For nonfloored p, r=||p|| and z=p/r, full Jacobian is (I-zz^T)/r, detached-denominator Jacobian I/r. Forwards agree at a fixed state while radial gradient components differ through this channel. This is conditional algebra, not measured backward evidence or removal of all normalization gradients. Floored cases require separate checks.
prior_work_and_difference.tested_difference: Round 6 supplies a forward-matched training derivative intervention for each pairing and a same-body raw bridge. Product normalization/replacement is distinct from log-count attention correction and softmax removal.

observations.observation: All 25 supplied trajectories succeeded operationally. Full and half count correction both lose DIN AUC. Half pooling improves on ordinary pooling but remains below DIN; full pooling correction loses AUC. These are scientific negatives or limited successes, not execution failures. No hidden failures are inferred.

The joint round-3 restriction gains 0.001162954694291618 AUC over its ordinary adapter. Cross-field removal alone nearly matches it. Context and cross-field restrictions interact; individual removal gains are not additive. Same-seed round-4 consistency and the round-6 raw bridge do not eliminate the small ordinary-adapter versus original-DIN offset.

Normalized aligned full-gradient remains the validation incumbent: AUC 0.6149816911798147 and Logloss 0.19656340759133067. It exceeds raw aligned by 0.0004876567525730069 AUC. Alignment beats crossed replacement under raw, unit-full and unit-detached rules at this seed.

Latest identity-gradient AUC is 0.6135629923558267; tangent-gradient AUC is 0.6140637917286534. Both lose AUC and Logloss to the incumbent. Tangent beats identity AUC but has worse Logloss; detached beats tangent AUC and Logloss. All remain seed-42 observations.

The aligned four-arm AUC ordering is full > detached > tangent > identity. Inverse-norm scaling gains 0.0010203397523019797 without projection and 0.0009178994511612748 with projection. Projection gains 0.0005007993728267657 without scaling and 0.00039835907168606077 with scaling. AUC interaction is -0.0001024403011407049.

Logloss does not follow the same factor ordering: projection without scaling worsens loss by 0.00002937708836051045, while projection with scaling improves it by 0.0000731807251322103. Scaling without projection changes loss by +0.00000029026315062630204, with no precision estimate; scaling with projection improves it by 0.00010226755034209445. Loss interaction is -0.00010255781349272075.

Both new arms report same-state full/surrogate product and logit max absolute differences of zero. On the first 512 validation impressions: 508 nonempty, 4 empty, 60,475 valid visible events, zero sampled floored events; zero padding mass and empty summaries. These are candidate-supplied forward checks, not independently verified backward tests.

The incumbent is not uniformly best across slices. Tangent slightly wins both metrics in history_1_16 (41,805 samples, 1,444 positives); raw wins both in history_17_64 (157,391 samples, 6,311 positives) and highest training-frequency group (1,004,912 samples, 33,140 positives). Empty-history AUC and Logloss ranks differ despite zero direct summaries.

All detailed history interaction arms have 17,130,275 parameters. Latest identity/tangent training times are 500.0755941569805/506.70840303599834 seconds and peak GPU bytes 800,977,920/834,704,896; full is 524.601099088788 seconds and 832,739,328 bytes. Inference is about 179k-180k examples/second for these three runs, including causal gathering, batch size 4096. No equal-compute or serving advantage is established.

interpretations.claim: The four-arm design provides provisional local evidence that both inverse-norm scaling and radial-component removal in the product-channel backward rule can affect validation ranking; their joint full rule is best at seed 42.
interpretations.qualification: Conditional on receipt-described implementation isolation. No source bodies or measured backward derivatives are available. Training trajectories and selected checkpoints differ. Factor effects are empirical contrasts, not a decomposition of a single fitted model or proof of semantic causality.

interpretations.claim: A forward-value-only explanation is insufficient for the reported full-versus-surrogate training outcomes if the specified source intervention is isolated: forwards agree at fixed states in the sampled diagnostics while trained outcomes differ.
interpretations.qualification: Limited sampled forward consistency; cannot infer full-population identity, initialization matching, exact optimizer updates or backward correctness. Other shared paths continue learning.

interpretations.claim: The latest unsuccessful variants refine rather than refute the normalization direction. Tangent-only or identity backward rules fail to improve the incumbent; raw/unit forward differences and training rules remain distinct mechanisms.
interpretations.qualification: No universal failure claim from one implementation and seed; no post-hoc normalization-strength or learning-rate search justified automatically.

interpretations.claim: Inverse-norm scaling has the larger observed AUC contrasts in this four-arm comparison, but this is compatible with effective step conditioning and shared embedding adaptation rather than a uniquely identified relevance mechanism.
interpretations.qualification: Do not describe factor deltas as a percentage of the gain explained or replace per-event scaling with its mean. Loss counterexamples and single-seed selection prevent a general ranking of mechanisms.

interpretations.claim: Earlier pairing and restriction results still support local structure-dependent behavior. They do not establish that category/brand semantics, attention mass, or removal of all context caused the improvement.
interpretations.qualification: Other scorer blocks/history values retain information, crossed coordinate distributions differ, and latest gradients were tested for aligned pairing only.

falsifiers.claim: Both gradient factors universally improve AUC and probability loss.
falsifiers.assessment: Already contradicted for probability loss: projection without scaling worsens Logloss; scaling without projection does not improve it at this seed. Crossed full versus detached also worsens Logloss.

falsifiers.claim: Full-rule advantage, the direction of each AUC factor effect and the interaction repeat across seeds.
falsifiers.assessment: Untested. Nonpositive paired mean effects or reversals in both new seeds weaken the corresponding robustness claim. Unstable interaction signs are inconclusive about general interaction, not a reason to relabel the original result.

falsifiers.claim: The intended backward intervention is isolated and correct.
falsifiers.assessment: Unequal fixed-state forwards, extra configuration or initialization changes, or product-channel derivatives inconsistent with the declared rule would invalidate attribution until resolved. Candidate forward checks cannot falsify a backward error.

falsifiers.claim: Full normalization is necessary for every local improvement or is uniformly best.
falsifiers.assessment: Already contradicted: detached exceeds raw on overall AUC, and raw/tangent win specified slices. Neither necessity nor uniformity follows from the incumbent rank.

falsifiers.claim: Matching attention mass establishes event relevance or semantic mediation.
falsifiers.assessment: Not tested. The diagnostics have no relevance labels and are off-policy fixed-state substitutions for inactive variants; matched norm does not match Jacobians or learned coordinate distributions.

prior_work_and_difference.local_algebra: For product p, r=||p||_2 and z=p/r on nonfloored events, P=I-zz^T. Unit forward z is common to I(identity), T(tangent), D(detached denominator) and F(full). Intended product-channel Jacobians: I: I; T: P; D: I/r; F: P/r. Upstream embedding gradients include product derivatives and other shared paths; these matrices are not whole-model Jacobians. Raw aligned/crossed products and the earlier D+X+C restriction algebra are described in the inherited record below.
prior_work_and_difference.gradient_hypothesis: Latest two arms complete the 2x2 inverse-norm scaling by tangent-projection training-rule factorial. Analytic nonfloored matrices describe intended semantics, not independently measured autograd. The exact epsilon/floor and surrogate floor derivative are unexposed and require source/host checks.
prior_work_and_difference.tested_difference: The latest registered identity and tangent surrogate backward rules preserve unit aligned forwards at a fixed state; full and detached corners come from prior rounds. No added learned parameters per receipts. Distinct from changing the product forward, log-count correction or introducing a new architecture.

prior_work_and_difference.inherited_round6_algebra: Let D=q_c*h_c+q_b*h_b, X=q_c*h_b+q_b*h_c, C=(q_c+q_b)*u, with * elementwise and u action/recency context. Ordinary product block is D+X+C. Round-3 cross_only REMOVES X and retains D+C; it is not the round-5/6 crossed replacement X alone. Unit normalization is z=p/max(||p||_2,epsilon), with p=D or X; exact floor constant is unexposed. Latest detached intervention stops only the denominator derivative. Other blocks/history values retain context and mixed-field information. No new parameters are added.

observations.statement: Useful history references: pooling adds 0.005222499224244892 AUC over static; target-aware DIN-style pooling adds 0.0031358724110027714 over simple pooling. Both lower Logloss. This does not isolate a field or behavior bottleneck.

Full behavior-count correction loses AUC and worsens Logloss for both pooling and DIN. Half correction improves pooling but still loses DIN AUC and Logloss. A discriminating weaker-strength follow-up was tried; these are successful executions with negative scientific outcomes. No combined count/product experiment exists.

The round-3 joint product restriction improves AUC by 0.001162954694291618 versus its ordinary adapter. Cross removal alone helps both metrics; context removal adds AUC with a Logloss penalty. AUC interaction is subadditive. Round-4 replay and inline implementations retain the gains. The ordinary-adapter offset from historical DIN persists; reproduction does not identify its cause.

Aligned unit products improve AUC by 0.0004876567525730069 and Logloss by -0.00012701821779648181 over aligned raw products. Aligned versus crossed replacements favor alignment in raw, unit/full-gradient and unit/detached-gradient settings. Norm-matched forward directions still differ; this does not isolate semantic alignment from representation/optimization.

Earlier projection AUC contrasts are positive at scale 1, event inverse norm, and constant .2, with strongly different magnitudes. Moderate constant scaling attains the adaptive full-rule AUC numerically, while the loss ranking favors full. The earlier adaptive-superiority explanation requires qualification.

Latest full replay exactly retains AUC 0.6149816911798147 and Logloss 0.19656340759133067; constant replay retains AUC 0.6149888455418249 and Logloss 0.1965762552803662. Both exactly reproduce all 23 prior slices. These are seed-42 bridges, not new random initializations.

Within-history scale reassignment has AUC 0.6147298332575719: -0.0002518579222428041 versus full, with Logloss worse by 0.00002158888593131736. It loses AUC in 22/23 overlapping reported slices; length 17-64 is the exception. The intervention is scientifically negative at this seed, not an execution failure.

History-mean scaling has AUC 0.6149872680212398: +0.000005576841425103396 versus full, -0.0000015775205850498963 versus constant. It worsens Logloss by 0.00004208375258465957 versus full. Mean beats reassignment in AUC by 0.0002574347636679075 but has worse Logloss by 0.000020494866653342214. Neither a new practical winner nor equivalence is established.

The latest diagnostic sample has 512 ordered impressions, 60475 regular valid events, 4 empty histories, 508 eligible rows, and only one singleton row. It reports zero same-state full/active product and logit differences, zero padding mass and empty summaries, and weight-sum error at most 1.7881393432617188e-7. No natural floored/boundary events occur. Reported synthetic VJP relative/scaled errors are at most 3.601953077337613e-15; these are candidate-supplied checks, not an independent audit of every training update.

At the reassigned checkpoint, within-history inverse-norm SD is 0.046375468373298645 and own/reassigned correlation is -0.0865853950381279. Reassignment changes own scales by mean absolute 0.05087236315011978 and preserves row scale sums/squared sums within relative errors 1.8293478376563144e-7/1.737557369096976e-7. At the mean checkpoint, averaging changes own scales by 0.03508317098021507 and preserves row sums within relative error 1.0340424694277317e-7. These checks show numerical activity on sampled states, not matched gradient/update energy across trained models.

Mean loses empty-history AUC by 0.00503257408172697 (8272 samples, 310 positives), short-history AUC by 0.0008312016598673866 (41805, 1444), and frequency-1-2 AUC by 0.0033862586845859743 (16534, 1045) versus full. Mean lowers Logloss in only one reported slice. Constant also has subgroup reversals. Shared retraining can change empty-history predictions even with zero empty summary; no per-empty-row causal effect follows.

All 32 authorized trials have detailed receipts, operational success and null errors. No failed host experiment is exposed. Count balancing, unscaled gradients, crossed replacements and reassignment remain as negative or inferior trajectories rather than being erased. Missing sources, tool-output truncation, and unavailable rg are distinct from scientific counterevidence.

interpretations.statement: When heterogeneous event scales are retained, assigning them to different events can harm the observed optimization trajectory. Averaging them instead retains the numerical AUC level at this seed. Correct per-event inverse norm is therefore not uniquely necessary for this observed AUC; harmful reassignment and useful adaptivity are different claims.
interpretations.qualification: One deterministic reassignment and one seed. No semantic relevance, general necessity, sufficiency, equivalence, or repeated-support claim.

interpretations.statement: The full-versus-reassigned difference is a conditional local performance contrast after approximately preserving within-history scale moments. Its interpretation is narrower than a general benefit of adaptivity.
interpretations.qualification: Controlled performance evidence conditional on receipt-described source isolation. Different checkpoints, gradient-direction correlations, temporal/action associations and Adam states remain; no identified mechanism.

interpretations.statement: Moderate product-channel backward scaling or reduced within-history variation is a plausible optimization explanation. The mean and constant replacements weaken the claim that precise event-specific scale assignment is needed for ranking.
interpretations.qualification: Adaptive/full still has the best observed Logloss among the latest four. Tiny AUC differences may be seed/search variation; loss divergence alone does not diagnose calibration.

interpretations.statement: Behavior-count normalization and product-gradient normalization are distinct interventions. Negative count results do not refute all multi-behavior modeling; aligned-product gains do not rescue the abandoned balancing hypothesis.
Earlier projection-by-scale effects remain conditional single-seed evidence. The latest experiment keeps tangent projection and does not independently test projection or interaction.

alternatives.explanation: Seed-specific optimization, checkpoint selection and adaptive reuse of validation can explain tiny mean/full/constant AUC differences.
alternatives.discriminating_check: Two new paired seeds for a fixed suite; report every seed, not only improved ones. User-cluster intervals need authorized predictions and user IDs.

alternatives.explanation: A reassignment rule may systematically alter time/action associations or create anticorrelation; its penalty need not demonstrate beneficial semantic scaling.
alternatives.discriminating_check: First repeat the existing rule; if stable and consequential, a separate prospectively declared multiple-permutation or action/time-stratified reassignment contrast can distinguish rule-specific effects. Do not add a sweep here.

alternatives.explanation: Preserving scale sums and squared sums does not preserve the norm of summed gradients, optimizer moments, clipping, directional alignment or update energy. Averaging also removes scale variance.

observations.statement: The three references rank static < pooled < target-aware DIN-style in full validation AUC (0.6050036144838207, 0.6102261137080656, 0.6133619861190683); both history additions lower Logloss. This establishes useful history information locally, not a particular semantic bottleneck.

All 34 allowed trial receipts report success with null errors; previous_runtime_error is null. Negative performance is distinct from execution failure. No additional failed or abandoned execution is invented.

Full behavior-count correction loses AUC and worsens Logloss for both pooling and DIN. Half correction improves pooling, but DIN still trails ordinary and full correction on AUC. The weaker-strength follow-up was informative and unsuccessful for DIN; count correction and product-gradient scaling are distinct interventions.

The round-3 aligned product restriction gains 0.001162954694291618 AUC over the ordinary adapter; removing cross products alone nearly recovers the gain. Removing context products alone improves AUC but worsens loss. Single removals interact subadditively on AUC. Same-seed replay/inline bridges preserve metrics but do not explain the ordinary-adapter versus original-DIN offset.

Aligned unit products beat aligned raw by 0.0004876567525730069 AUC and lower Logloss. The crossed replacement obtains almost no AUC gain from normalization and worsens loss. Alignment remains favored with unit norms and with detached denominator gradients. Scalar product magnitude alone is not an adequate account, conditional on implementation isolation; semantic causality remains unestablished.

Backward controls have identical reported same-state forward values but different trained outcomes. Projection helps AUC at unscaled, event inverse-norm and fixed 0.2 scales, with different magnitudes. Fixed scaling nearly matches full-rule AUC; the earlier interpretation that exact event-adaptive scaling is necessary is weakened. Full remains lower in Logloss.

Round-9 full and fixed replays exactly reproduce prior AUC, Logloss and 23 slices. Whole-history reassignment loses AUC and loss versus full. Whole-history mean gives AUC 0.6149872680212398, numerically near fixed/full but with worse loss; no equivalence or independent repetition follows.

Latest action mean: AUC 0.614672318575737, Logloss 0.19661644463258673. Relative to full, AUC falls 0.0003093726040777067 and loss rises 0.0000530370412560599. It also trails whole-history mean on both metrics. This is negative evidence for this action-conditioned averaging implementation.

Latest within-action reassignment: AUC 0.6147849008671875, Logloss 0.19668868647099816. Relative to full, AUC falls 0.00019679031262720414 and loss rises 0.0001252788796674842. Compared with whole-history reassignment, AUC improves 0.00005506760961559998 while loss worsens 0.00010368999373616683; AUC-only partial recovery is not a general rescue.

The mean-minus-reassignment AUC contrast changes from +0.0002574347636679075 across whole histories to -0.00011258229145050258 within action groups. Grouping-by-operation AUC difference in differences is -0.0003700170551184101; corresponding Logloss contrast is -0.0000927367050647665. Mean has lower loss than reassignment in both groupings. The interaction is descriptive at seed 42, not a semantic decomposition.

Neither latest arm improves the incumbent: action mean/fixed AUC delta -0.00031652696608786; action reassigned/fixed -0.00020394467463735744, both with worse loss. Both still exceed original DIN at this seed; inherited architecture gains cannot be attributed to the new grouping intervention.

Each latest arm loses AUC in 21 of 23 overlapping slices versus full and has worse Logloss in all 23. Action mean improves AUC only in history lengths 1-16 and 17-64; action reassignment only in lengths 17-64 and hour 6-12. These slice counts are exploratory, not independent statistical votes.

Latest diagnostics report 512 ordered validation impressions, 60475 regular events, 4 empty histories, no natural floor/boundary cases, and action-code event counts 57171/1634/650/1020. Own/action reassigned correlation is about -0.103; the reassignment changes about 96.15% of eligible scales. Group sums and reassigned squared sums are preserved in sampled states to roughly 2.1e-7 relative error. Moment preservation does not preserve gradient norms or optimizer updates.

Latest candidate diagnostics report zero same-state full/active forward product and logit differences; zero padding mass and empty summaries. Synthetic VJP audits now report errors at most 3.602e-15 across six modes, with one boundary and four floored synthetic events and only two probes per mode. Submission notes said these measurements were unknown at submission; committed diagnostic results now exist. These remain candidate-supplied bounded checks, not an independent audit of training updates.

Latest arms and closest history controls all have 17130275 parameters (17078688 embeddings, 51587 dense). Action mean/reassignment wall time is 620.45/622.35 seconds, train time 529.88/532.86 seconds, peak memory approximately 835.10 MB. Latest faster inference measurements relative to round 9 do not establish efficiency: recipes are matched, but round-specific gathering, scheduling and diagnostics can vary.

interpretations.statement: Grouping and scale operation interact on observed ranking. Action-conditioned averaging underperforms whole-history averaging, while restricting reassignment gives a small AUC recovery and worsens loss. A general claim that finer action-specific allocation helps is unsupported.

interpretations.statement: Moderate shared scaling remains a plausible optimizer-conditioning explanation. Near-best AUC from full, fixed and whole-history mean does not imply identical mechanisms or performance equivalence. Action mean failure weakens the stronger assertion that any averaging replacement suffices.

Preserved action-wise scale moments plus nonzero reassignment activity narrow a scalar-marginal explanation, but do not identify semantic relevance. Norm-direction association, temporal order, cross-action update coupling and Adam moments remain possible mediators.

Constant tangent remains the numerical AUC incumbent. Its approximately 7.15e-6 AUC advantage over full is preliminary; full has lower Logloss. No practical superiority, significance, calibration diagnosis, robustness, external novelty or final-assessment success is established.

candidate_diagnostics.scope: Candidate-supplied diagnostics on the ordered first 512 validation impressions at separately trained checkpoints; 60475 valid events and 4 empty histories. Neither population estimates nor independent training-gradient audits.
candidate_diagnostics.checks: Both report zero same-state full/active product and logit differences, zero padding mass and empty summaries. Eight-mode synthetic VJPs now have reported relative-scaled errors <=3.602e-15, with 2 probes per mode, 1 synthetic boundary and 4 floored valid cases. Notes describing these measurements as unknown were prospective submission notes; committed diagnostic outcomes now exist.
candidate_diagnostics.caution: No natural floor/boundary cases in this ordered sample. Scale-sum/squared-sum conservation does not conserve summed gradient norms, Adam moments or update energy. Checkpoint correlation/distance comparisons are consequences of different training trajectories.

slice_analysis.status: All inherited 23 slice definitions and current comparisons are exploratory; no post-hoc bin fitting or independent statistical votes. Counts checked identical across trials. Original exact bin construction is not fully exported.
slice_analysis.insufficiency: Empty history has only 310 positives despite 8272 impressions; rare subgroups and ordered first-512 events cannot establish mechanism precision. No invented sufficiency threshold. User clustering, intervals and multiplicity adjustments are unavailable from aggregates.
slice_analysis.missing_coverage: Training-frequency groups are present, but full missing/unseen-field population slices are not exported; diagnostic target-brand zeros do not substitute for them. No events beyond the 128-event cap are observed.

observations.statement: Feature-only, pooled and target-aware references have AUC 0.6050036145, 0.6102261137 and 0.6133619861; both history additions reduce Logloss. This establishes local predictive value of history, without diagnosing a specific semantic limitation.
All 36 allowed attempts succeeded with null errors; previous_runtime_error is null. No unobserved execution failure is invented. Negative scientific results are retained below.

Full action-count correction loses AUC and worsens loss for pooling and DIN. A weaker half correction improves pooling but still lowers DIN AUC. This unsuccessful follow-up does not refute all multi-behavior modeling and is distinct from product-gradient scaling.

Joint removal of off-diagonal category-brand and target-context products gains 0.0011629547 AUC against the ordinary adapter; cross-product removal alone nearly attains that gain. Context removal alone improves AUC but worsens loss. The AUC interaction is subadditive. Deterministic bridges leave a small ordinary-adapter/original-DIN offset unresolved.

Aligned unit products improve over aligned raw by 0.0004876568 AUC and lower loss. Normalization gives only 0.0000139449 AUC to crossed products and worsens loss. Alignment also wins with detached denominator gradients. Product magnitude alone is insufficient as an explanation conditional on source isolation; semantic causality is unestablished.

Backward-only controls report matched same-state forward values but different learned outcomes. Projection improves AUC at unscaled, inverse-norm and constant 0.2 scales, with scale-dependent contrasts. Constant scaling nearly matches full AUC while full has lower loss; exact own-event scaling is not uniquely required for the recorded seed-42 ranking level.

Full/fixed deterministic replays exactly match AUC, Logloss and slices. Whole-history mean is numerically near full/fixed AUC with worse loss; whole-history half-rotation loses AUC and loss. Replay equality and numerical closeness are neither independent repetition nor equivalence.

Action-wise mean underperforms history mean on both metrics. Action-wise half-rotation recovers 0.0000550676 AUC relative to history half-rotation but worsens loss by 0.0001036900 and still trails full. Grouping reverses the mean-minus-half AUC sign; its difference in differences is -0.0003700171.

Action-adjacent gives AUC 0.6149537731900387 and Logloss 0.1965878918767361. Versus action half-rotation: AUC +0.00016887232285123233, loss -0.00010079459426207138. It still trails full and fixed AUC and has worse loss than both.

History-adjacent is the new numerical AUC maximum, +9.8962003826086331e-06 above the previous fixed-scale incumbent, with loss worse by 8.0971968067777844e-06. Action-adjacent minus history-adjacent AUC is -4.4968552168733744e-05. The action-minus-history adjacent-versus-half AUC interaction is -0.00010003616178433372; the corresponding loss interaction is -0.00010015059417306515.

Both latest arms exceed original DIN AUC at seed 42. History-adjacent minus DIN is +0.0016367556231391411 AUC and has lower loss; this combined lineage gain cannot all be attributed to the latest donor change.

History-adjacent wins AUC in 10/23 overlapping slices against full and loss in 4/23; action-adjacent wins 7/23 and 2/23. History-adjacent empty-history AUC is 0.5764913581 versus full 0.5839558467 (delta -0.0074644886), with loss +0.0007375294; only 310 positives are in that slice. Shared parameters can change empty-history predictions even when the local empty summary stays zero.

History-adjacent loses AUC in the >64-history slice by 0.0000208289 despite winning full-population AUC. AUC is not an additive average of slice AUCs; cross-slice positive-negative ordering also contributes. No mechanism attribution follows from this apparent aggregate/slice difference.

Latest ordered-checkpoint diagnostics report original-to-assigned centered scale correlations 0.55634 (history) and 0.50954 (action), versus half-offset comparators -0.08553 and -0.10724 at those same states. Mean absolute donor index gaps are 1.983/3.206 versus 62.392/61.133, and donor age gaps 6369.81/10255.54 seconds versus 174352.92/171055.83. The adjacent rule changes >95% of scales relative to half in the sample.

History-adjacent transports about 9.536% of sampled scales across action labels; action-adjacent transports none. Sampled scale sums and squared sums are preserved to <=1.778e-7 relative error. Action-code counts are 57171/1634/650/1020, so these diagnostics predominantly concern the common behavior.

Committed synthetic eight-mode VJP checks report errors <=3.602e-15 and zero forward discrepancies. These candidate-authored probes support bounded implementation activity/correctness, not independent attribution or population gradient/update behavior. Floor/boundary events occur synthetically but not naturally in the 512-row sample.

Both latest models and close controls have 17130275 parameters (17078688 embedding, 51587 dense). History/action adjacent wall seconds are 599.56/616.45 and train seconds 511.73/528.06; peak memory is about 835.10 MB. Relative speed differences are descriptive; no equal-compute frontier or reliable runtime advantage has been measured.

interpretations.statement: The donor reassignment rule matters locally: a nearby donor recovers the AUC lost under half-rotation in both tested groupings. The earlier half-rotation penalty does not establish that all scale reassignment is harmful.
interpretations.qualification: Two controlled local contrasts conditional on receipt-described isolation. Same seed and two deterministic donor rules only; no repeated mechanism support.

interpretations.statement: A blanket need to preserve exact own-event inverse norm is weakened by full, fixed, whole-history mean and history-adjacent AUC proximity. The full derivative retains the best observed Logloss.
interpretations.qualification: No equivalence/noninferiority margin or cross-seed precision; adaptive validation selection can dominate tiny rankings.

interpretations.statement: Preserving action membership alone does not explain recovery: action half-rotation remains below full while history-adjacent recovers AUC with nonzero cross-action donation. This is limited evidence against action preservation as the sole sufficient/necessary account for these implementations.
interpretations.qualification: Do not generalize necessity/sufficiency beyond these observed rules and seed; time/order/norm correlations remain confounded.

interpretations.statement: Temporal proximity, high own-to-donor scale correlation and scale-to-gradient-direction covariance are plausible accounts of the adjacent-versus-half contrast, but are not separated. Short donor age/index gaps and positive scale correlation co-occur; learned checkpoint statistics are downstream of optimization.
interpretations.qualification: No claim that temporal semantics, causal interest relevance or an optimal locality radius has been identified.

interpretations.statement: Grouping interacts with donor operation at seed 42, while earlier mean-versus-half interaction and negative action-mean outcomes remain valid local observations. The latest contrast revises the interpretation of reassignment, without erasing those outcomes.
interpretations.qualification: Mixed-round controlled performance contrasts; independent source verification and paired repetitions remain necessary.

interpretations.statement: The selected AUC leader has no demonstrated practical or universal advantage over fixed/full. Its loss and empty-history penalties must accompany its primary metric selection.
interpretations.qualification: Numerical selection under the frozen metric, not significance or final scientific success.

candidate_diagnostics.interpretation: At the scale-half checkpoint, rank-adjacent scale correlation is about +0.899 versus -0.345 for rank-half, with mean age gaps about 48405 versus 125347 seconds. Rank-half also has larger own/donor scale differences. Its numerical AUC win therefore does not support a monotonic positive-correlation or temporal-locality explanation. These statistics are downstream of training and cannot measure mediation. Conserving scalar moments does not conserve total gradient norm, shared-embedding accumulation, update energy or Adam state.

observations.statement: Feature-only, pooled and target-aware reference AUCs are 0.6050036145, 0.6102261137 and 0.6133619861; history additions reduce Logloss. This establishes useful predictive history signal without identifying a semantic limitation.
All 39 allowed model trials succeeded and have null errors; previous_runtime_error is null. Scientific negative and abandoned branches remain evidence; no unseen execution failures are invented.
Full count correction reduces pooled and DIN AUC. Half correction helps pooling by 0.0005804055 but reduces DIN AUC by 0.0002082243; partial correction did not rescue this target-aware branch.

Aligned raw products improve the ordinary product adapter by 0.0011629547 AUC; the ordinary adapter itself remains slightly below original DIN. Removing only off-diagonal products also helps, so both restrictions cannot receive undivided credit. Same-seed round-4/raw bridges reproduce these aggregates.

Unit normalization helps aligned AUC by 0.0004876568; crossed unit normalization barely changes AUC and worsens loss. Aligned exceeds crossed at equal unit norm, weakening a solely explicit product-magnitude explanation but leaving field/coordinate/optimization explanations.

Full aligned derivative exceeds detached, tangent-only and identity surrogate AUC in the original gradient factorial, but fixed 0.2 tangent and identity surrogates later approach the full result. Exact adaptive scale or projection necessity is not established.

Whole-history mean retains AUC near full/fixed but worsens Logloss. Chronological half-rotation loses AUC; action mean and action-half controls do not rescue it. Chronological adjacent recovers AUC in both groupings. Retain the negative branches and the rule-specific nature of that recovery.
The latest chronological-half bridge exactly reproduces r0009-history_reassigned AUC, Logloss and all slices. It is a deterministic lineage check, not a new seed.

Inverse-norm rank adjacent and half have AUCs 0.6150251061 and 0.6151021885. Scale-half exceeds the previous incumbent by 0.0001034468, full by 0.0001204973 and fixed by 0.0001133430; its Logloss also improves against all three. Scale-adjacent has the lowest recorded Logloss 0.1965201288. Both latest leaders remain seed-42 exploratory results.

Chronological adjacent-minus-half AUC is +0.0002689085; rank adjacent-minus-half is -0.0000770824. The rank-minus-chronological interaction is -0.0003459909. Rank ordering improves both offsets, more strongly for half. Adjacent has lower Logloss than half in both orders, so AUC and loss do not share the same ordering interaction.

The latest rules retain 17130275 parameters, including 51587 dense parameters; wall times are 635.69 and 639.45 seconds and peak memory 835099136 bytes. Cost is measured descriptively; equal parameter counts/data passes do not establish equal compute.

interpretations.statement: The supplied ordering-by-offset factorial gives provisional local evidence that the allocation of backward scale across events matters under this fixed forward model; a universal penalty for half-rotation is inconsistent with the newest rankings.
interpretations.qualification: Conditional on receipt-described common forward and isolated derivative. One training seed and adaptive validation reuse; no repeated mechanism support.

interpretations.statement: The earlier adjacent recovery cannot be attributed simply to temporal proximity or high positive own/donor scale correlation. The rank-half AUC leader uses a more distant, negatively correlated donor in the sampled diagnostics; positive correlation is not a demonstrated necessary condition for this numerical recovery.
interpretations.qualification: No monotonic correlation or distance mechanism has been isolated. Rank, tie handling, recipient direction and shared optimizer effects remain coupled.

interpretations.statement: Rank-based reassignment may alter scale-to-gradient-direction coupling or act as regularization while preserving the scalar scale distribution. Neither explanation is identified; negative correlation itself is not established as beneficial.
interpretations.qualification: No measured training gradients, gradient norms, update trajectories or fixed-state population probes. Scale moments do not match optimizer dynamics.

interpretations.statement: Action membership alone was already inadequate to explain the chronology-half penalty; the new whole-history rank result does not establish a special multi-behavior semantic interaction or repair of action imbalance.
interpretations.qualification: The rank-by-offset factorial varies order within histories, not action grouping, so no rank-by-action or higher-order interaction is identified.

interpretations.statement: Scale-half is the current primary-metric incumbent and scale-adjacent is a relevant quality/cost alternative, but neither has demonstrated reliable superiority across seeds, all slices or held-out data.
interpretations.qualification: Metric disagreement alone does not establish calibration; slice counts and uncertainty remain material.

limitations: Only seed 42 is observed. Deterministic replays are not independent repetitions. Adaptive validation reuse can inflate selected differences; no statistical significance, equivalence, noninferiority or repeated mechanism support.

Actual sources/checkpoints/raw data/individual predictions are not exported. Hashes and notes preserve provenance but do not independently verify identical construction, initial tensors, data order, checkpoint policy or backward isolation.

New factorial uses stable inverse-norm ordering and two deterministic offsets, not random independent donor contrasts. Rank ties, temporal distance, behavior membership, scale correlation and scale-direction pairing remain coupled. No optimal radius or causal temporal/semantic mechanism is identified.

Scale first/second-moment conservation leaves accumulated gradient norms, optimizer moments and update energy unmatched; group means remove variance. New rules hold projection fixed and do not identify projection-by-rank or action-by-rank interactions.

Candidate-authored diagnostics cover first 512 ordered impressions with only four empty histories and no natural floored/boundary events. Two synthetic probes per mode are bounded checks, not independent training/device/dtype verification.

All 23 overlapping slices are exploratory. Exposures are not independent users; cluster intervals are unavailable. Missing/unseen full-population slices and untruncated histories beyond the 128-event cap are unobserved.
AUC/loss tradeoffs alone do not diagnose calibration. Aggregate AUC is not a weighted average of slice AUC. Empty-history differences may arise through shared learned embeddings.

The ordinary product adapter differs numerically from original DIN despite exact bridges. Published DIN omits attention-output softmax; this local masked-softmax reference is an adaptation, not an exact reproduction.
Publisher static user/ad snapshot dates are undocumented. Readiness and causal/scorer checks are inherited from the frozen host protocol; no independent production point-in-time guarantee.

Equal parameters and passes do not imply equal compute. Allocated GPU seconds, exact training examples processed, repeated latency benchmark, equal-compute frontier and actual closed-scoring costs are not exported.

All exposed trials succeeded operationally; scientific negative outcomes and abandoned count/crossed/identity/action-mean branches remain recorded. Preparation harness/retrieval issues are distinct from model failures and remain charged.

Closest external normalization/surrogate-gradient prior work remains unverified. Empty bounded registry search does not establish novelty. Industry cards are external reports, considered but not implemented; no transfer or causal knowledge-value claim.
